svg.aria-label: os-xgs-npu status. Stage: discovery, front ports, offload and integration done, the work-in-progress notice lifted; what is left being completed as updates. XGS 3300, Cavium OCTEON TX and CN83XX: Front ports: 12 of 12, and the module's; Receive: an interrupt per ring; Transmit: seven rings; Flow table: 2,000,000, the board's; Flow writes: posted, no wait; IPv6 flows: in hardware; Handed back: revived in place; IPsec: GCM and CBC and NAT-T and IPv6; Tunnel flows: outbound, in hardware; Appliance: sensors and panel and watchdog; IPv6, flows in hardware: 9.24 and 9.27 Gbit/s; IPsec, MTU 9000: 7.41 Gbit/s, one stream; Flow table: 99.6 % of frames in hardware; weighted completion 96 per cent. XGS 136, Marvell CN9131 and ARMADA: Front ports: 14 of 14; Receive: polled every millisecond; Transmit: four queues; Flow table: 1,500,000, the board's; Flow writes: each one waited for; IPv6 flows: built, not measured; Handed back: revived in place; IPsec: GCM and CBC and NAT-T, no IPv6; Tunnel flows: not built; Appliance: sensors and PoE read and watchdog; Flows in hardware: 941 and 914 Mbit/s, CPU 0.4 %; IPsec, MTU 9000: 982 Mbit/s, link-bound; Four transmit queues: 941 Mbit/s, all in use; weighted completion 91 per cent. OCTEON TX2 and TX2 98XX described only; TOPAZ and GR have no coprocessor. 2,391 GiB over TLS, not a byte changed; 6,100 give-backs revived, none refused; 10 and 19 claims withdrawn and dead ends recorded.
svg.text: WHAT RUNS ON EACH APPLIANCE, AND HOW FAR ALONG IT IS
“The main part is done; what is left arrives as updates.”
The same features on both cards: a full circle is run on that appliance, a half is built or partial, an empty one is not built yet.
Every row is in docs/families/parity.md; every figure on a page in docs/measurements, with a photograph of the run.
